lead.headline: Tate lands on the injury report; Tuten is finally in
lead.deck: Your second receiver was limited on Thursday with a back nobody has explained. The lineup is the projection's for the first time this week, and Pickens plays tonight.
lead.body: Start with the bad news about your own players. Carnell Tate, who drew twelve targets last week and faces the defence that gives receivers more than any other, was added to Tennessee's injury report on Thursday afternoon: limited, back. He was not listed on Wednesday. No coach has spoken about it, nothing says how it happened, and Houston's copy of the report calls it a knee. The outlets that have guessed expect him to play if Friday goes well; that is a guess. Saquon Barkley missed practice again and has done no on-field work since the hamstring. Alvin Kamara, on your bench, did practise, limited. The better news is of your own making. At 08:44 this morning you put Bhayshul Tuten in the running-back slot Ollie Gordon had held since Tuesday, and your lineup is now the projection lineup: 118.8 against 117.5, with ESPN giving you 51% against Kings of the North, who have Tee Higgins in their flex at zero after he missed a second practice. George Pickens plays tonight at 18:15 in your flex, healthy, against a Tampa Bay defence missing three starters; the inactive list was not yet published when this went to press. One instruction is left for the week. At 09:30 on Sunday, read Tennessee's inactive list: if Tate is on it, Matthew Golden takes his slot. Golden kicks off at the same hour, so nothing needs deciding before then. Make no claim; you are last in the order. Roman Wilson is the one new name on the wire, free, with Pittman out for weeks and the same six targets every game.
